cards.text: Welcome to Sparkle's station, friend! A new section of Proverbs opens here, and the heading reads, "The proverbs of Solomon:" That's Solomon, son of David, king of Israel, and his sayings come two lines at a time, putting the wise and the foolish side by side.

cards.question: Solomon's very first proverb: "A wise son brings joy to his father, but a foolish son grief to his mother." What's the big point?

answers.text: A son's choices reach his whole family
A son's choices only affect himself
Parents decide how a son turns out

cards.text: Then Solomon talks money: "Ill-gotten treasures profit nothing," and that's worth less than the dead batteries I shared my old junk drawer with. At least THEY swore they had a little charge left!

cards.question: Solomon says ill-gotten treasures profit nothing, but righteousness brings deliverance from death. So when it really counts, doing ___ is worth more than piling up money.
True or false: Solomon says the LORD lets the righteous go hungry.

cards.text: Next, Solomon holds up two pairs of hands: idle hands make one poor, but diligent hands bring wealth. I pack cookie boxes with a MUSTACHE, friend, and even I know which pair I'd hire.

cards.question: Solomon says the son who gathers in summer is wise, but the son who sleeps during harvest is disgraceful. What's the lesson?

answers.text: Work while the work is ready
Rest whenever you feel worn out
Leave the harvest to hired hands

cards.text: Harvest is the ONE season you do not hit snooze, and I say that as a stamper who snoozed an oven timer once and smelled it for a week. Then Solomon says blessings are on the head of the righteous, but the mouth of the wicked conceals violence.

cards.question: Solomon says the memory of the righteous is a blessing, but the name of the wicked will rot. True or false: this proverb is about how people remember you.

cards.text: A wise heart will receive commandments, but foolish lips will come to ruin. That's the guy who talks all the way through the safety briefing and then asks where the exits are.

cards.question: Solomon says he who walks in integrity walks securely, but he who perverts his ways will be found out. The walking here is a picture of how a person ___.

cards.text: He who winks the eye causes grief, and then that line again: foolish lips will come to ruin. With eyebrows THIS big, I couldn't wink if I tried, so I'm in the clear on that one.

Then Solomon says the mouth of the righteous is a fountain of life, but the mouth of the wicked conceals violence. That second half is word for word from verse 6, because some lines are worth stamping twice.

cards.question: Solomon calls the mouth of the righteous a fountain of life. What's that picture saying?

answers.text: Their words are kept for later
Their words are hard to swallow

cards.text: Then hatred stirs up dissension, but love covers all transgressions. Hatred is one comment in the group chat, and suddenly forty people are typing.

Wisdom is found on the lips of the discerning, but a rod is for the back of him who lacks judgment, and OOF, Solomon does not tiptoe. The wise store up knowledge like chocolate chips before the holiday rush, but the mouth of the fool invites destruction.

cards.question: Look how often these proverbs bring up the mouth and the lips. Solomon keeps paying close attention to what people ___.
Solomon says the wealth of the rich man is his fortified city, but poverty is the ruin of the poor. True or false: the fortified city is a picture of money as protection.
Now back to the big contrast. The labor of the ___ leads to life, but the gain of the ___ brings punishment.

cards.text: Back at the counter, friend. Solomon says whoever heeds instruction is on the path to life.

cards.question: Solomon pictures heeding instruction as the path to life. True or false: he says the one who ignores reproof stays on that path too.

cards.text: Then Solomon says the one who conceals hatred has lying lips, and whoever spreads slander is a fool. That's the coworker who says "Love your shoes!" and then talks about your shoes all afternoon in the break room.

cards.question: Solomon says when words are many, sin is unavoidable. So the wise person keeps his lips ___.

cards.text: Somebody needs to tape that one RIGHT over the reply-all button, friend. Then Solomon says the tongue of the righteous is choice silver.

cards.question: Solomon calls the tongue of the righteous choice silver. What's that picture saying about their words?
Solomon says the lips of the righteous feed many, but fools die for lack of judgment. Their words do for people what food does: they ___ them.
True or false: Solomon says the blessing of the LORD enriches, but sorrow comes along with it.

cards.text: The fool delights in shameful conduct, but a man of understanding has wisdom. That's the guy bragging that he ran every red light on the way here, like he's showing off a trophy.

cards.question: Solomon says what the wicked man dreads will overtake him, but the desire of the righteous will be granted. What's he saying about the wicked man's fears?

answers.text: They are all in his head

cards.question: Then a whirlwind passes through. True or false: Solomon says the righteous get swept away along with the wicked.

cards.text: Then Solomon paints a picture that makes you squint: like vinegar to the teeth and smoke to the eyes.

cards.question: Vinegar to the teeth and smoke to the eyes. Who does Solomon say is like that to those who send him?

cards.text: The slacker: the coworker who says "On it!" and then you never hear from him again. Next, the fear of the LORD prolongs life, but the years of the wicked will be cut short.

cards.question: Solomon says the hope of the righteous is joy, but the expectations of the wicked will perish. What the wicked are counting on will come to ___.

cards.text: The way of the LORD is a refuge to the upright, but destruction awaits those who do evil. And the righteous will never be shaken, which is more than I can say for my chef's hat every time the oven door slams.

cards.question: Solomon says the way of the LORD is a refuge to the upright. What's that picture saying?

answers.text: The upright must hide from it

cards.question: Solomon says the mouth of the righteous brings forth wisdom, but a perverse tongue will be cut out. True or false: in Solomon's proverbs, what a person says carries real consequences.

cards.text: The lips of the righteous know what is fitting, but the mouth of the wicked is perverse. Mouths, lips and tongues ALL over this chapter, friend, and here I am with a giant mustache parked right over mine like a filter!

findings.problem: The card says Solomon is the son of David and king of Israel. That fact comes from Proverbs 1:1, which is outside the passage, but the card cites only Proverbs 10:1 and gives no reference for it.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The card says Solomon's sayings are 'putting the wise and the foolish side by side.' That isn't true of the whole chapter. Most proverbs here contrast the righteous and the wicked, and several contrast neither (10:10, 10:15, 10:18, 10:22, 10:26).

rule.text: What he points out must be true.

findings.problem: Verse 2 contrasts righteousness with ill-gotten treasures. The question changes this to 'piling up money' in general, which the text doesn't say. The same chapter also says diligent hands bring wealth (10:4) and that the LORD's blessing enriches (10:22).

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: The card says the second half of verse 6 is repeated in verse 11 'because some lines are worth stamping twice.' The text never says why the line repeats, so this adds a reason it doesn't give.

rule.text: He never adds why someone did, said or thought something unless the text says why.

findings.problem: This fill in the blank asks the baker to supply the missing words of the verse itself ('The labor of the ___ leads to life, but the gain of the ___ brings punishment'). That tests wording, not movement or meaning.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.
